question: On Friday 19 January 2024, Teresa Ribera, the third deputy prime minister of Spain, openly questioned the decisions of National High Court judge Manuel García Castellón in a terrorism case against former Catalan premier and current MEP Carles Puigdemont. Specifically, Ribera stated that the judge ‘is deeply involved in politics and tends to crop up at crunch times.

There are some people who have a certain penchant for always commenting along the same lines and at just the right times, compared with what we’d usually expect to hear from other colleagues within the judiciary’. The General Council of the Judiciary unanimously condemned these accusations as being ‘at odds with the principle of institutional loyalty’ and ‘the general duty of respecting judicial independence’.
In view of these serious comments by a member of the Spanish Government about a judge, I have the following questions: 1.
What is the Commission’s view on this attack on judicial independence?
What is the Commission going to do to protect the rule of law in Spain?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (5.4.2024) The Commission is aware of the issue raised by the Honourable Member. Already in 2022 and 2023 Country Chapters on the rule of law situation in Spain1, the Commission underlined that stakeholders had raised concerns of public statements by politicians, including members of Parliament and the Government, criticising the judiciary.

In this context, the Commission recalled that, ‘according to European standards, while courts are not immune to criticism and scrutiny, the judiciary must enjoy public confidence to be successful in view of its special role in society.

This is particularly important in relation to statements by members of the legislative and the executive branches, as all powers of the State must foster and protect the trust of the general public in constitutional institutions including the judiciary’2.

The Commission remains committed to taking any necessary measures to ensure compliance with EU law and upholding the rule of law in all Member States, and will continue to work with the Spanish authorities to promote the rule of law within the framework of the rule of law cycle.
